# Pack conformance — partial: 3 of 6 gates independently fixture-proven

**Partial conformance: 3 of 6 pack-fitness gates are independently fixture-proven.** There is deliberately no overall pass badge on this page. Passing the fixture harness is not the same as passing pack fitness: three invariants are checked only against the real tree, and a pack author learns those verdicts by submitting to CI, not by running a fixture.

## What each gate checks, and how you can check it

| Gate | Invariant | Mechanism | Evidence level | Blocking contract |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lint_pack_boundaries` | a markdown link may not cross into a pack the source pack does not require | fixture tree | fixture-proven | — |
| `lint_rule_skill_pack_reach` | a rule and the skills it routes to must arrive in the same pack-legal install | fixture tree | fixture-proven | — |
| `lint_pack_risk_class` | risk_class: high ⇒ default_install: false AND requires_explicit_consent: true AND surface_tier: lab | fixture predicate | fixture-proven | — |
| `lint_pack_dependencies` | the pack dependency graph is acyclic and every declared pack exists | real tree only | **CI-contract-only** | `main()` accepts no argv and the pack home is derived from `import.meta.url`. Effort-level, not design-level: nothing states the absence is intended. |
| `lint_pack_first_win` | a pack may not shadow an artefact another pack already wins | real tree only | **CI-contract-only** | the gate's CLI contract PINS argv-ignoring behaviour — its own header reads "the CLI contract is pinned — `main()` IGNORES argv entirely". Design-level: a port-fidelity guarantee from ADR-200, so a fixture seam needs that record amended. |
| `prove_pack_extractable` | a pack plus its declared closure is self-contained and liftable out | real tree only | **CI-contract-only** | `prove(pack)` resolves a pack BY NAME under the real `src/packs/`, so a fixture would have to be a real pack. Effort-level, but it changes an exported signature two tests already use. |

## The seeded twins — one violation each

Each twin overlays the conformant fixture and must red **exactly one** gate while the others stay green. That second half is the load-bearing one: a twin that reds two gates is not isolating an invariant, and a page built on it would attribute a failure to the wrong contract.

| Twin | Reds | What it seeds |
|---|---|---|
| `undeclared-cross-pack-link` | `lint_pack_boundaries` | the requires edge is dropped, so a skill link crosses an undeclared boundary |
| `unreachable-route` | `lint_rule_skill_pack_reach` | the requires edge is dropped, so a rule routes to a skill its install cannot receive |
| `high-risk-default-install` | `lint_pack_risk_class` | a risk_class: high pack ships default-on, consent-free, at a non-lab tier |

There are 3 twins, not 6: a twin is only meaningful for a gate a fixture can drive.

## Why three gates are not fixture-provable

The distinction below matters more than the count. **Design-level** means a contract deliberately forbids the seam; **effort-level** means nobody has built it and nothing says they should not. A pack author reading this should not treat the two as the same kind of gap.

- `lint_pack_dependencies` — `main()` accepts no argv and the pack home is derived from `import.meta.url`. Effort-level, not design-level: nothing states the absence is intended.
- `lint_pack_first_win` — the gate's CLI contract PINS argv-ignoring behaviour — its own header reads "the CLI contract is pinned — `main()` IGNORES argv entirely". Design-level: a port-fidelity guarantee from ADR-200, so a fixture seam needs that record amended.
- `prove_pack_extractable` — `prove(pack)` resolves a pack BY NAME under the real `src/packs/`, so a fixture would have to be a real pack. Effort-level, but it changes an exported signature two tests already use.

A partial temp-tree copy is not an escape: four of the six gates carry dead-scope assertions, so a skeleton holding only the fixture exits `2` ("scanned 0"), not `0`. Only a full tree copy per twin would satisfy them.

## How to run it

```bash
./scripts-run src/scripts/check_pack_conformance_fixture          # the harness
./scripts-run src/scripts/check_pack_conformance_fixture --emit-doc  # regenerate this page
```

Regenerating on an unchanged tree is a no-op, so `git diff --exit-code` over this file is the drift check.
